messages:
maya: Heads up — saw a 3x p99 latency spike on the dedicated inference pool during the 11:03 burst. Throughput dropped ~25% for ~2.5m. KV cache miss rate jumped from 4% -> 22% at the same time.
jin: same. traces show a bunch of requests falling back to the generic attention kernel around that window (arm-quant -> generic). Kernel selection logs show repeated kernel-compat checks failing.
ryan: paste of logs:
```
2029-11-02T11:03:12Z kernel_selector: model=rwkv-v2 variant=quant-arm compat_check=false fallback=generic
2029-11-02T11:03:13Z joiner: queued=78 draining=false
2029-11-02T11:03:15Z provisioner: pending_alloc=12 backoff_ms=1500
```
jin: looks like provisioner couldn't handoff GPU warm-forks quickly -> joiner queue piles up -> batching heuristic keeps forming tiny batches -> latency up.
maya: Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/serve/perf?orgId=1&from=1698860580000&to=1698860700000 — you can see the spike and the KV miss curve.
anita: I pulled the allocator metrics: provisioner queue latency spiked to 11s median, and instance-init success rate dropped 87%->61% for the short window. Also saw a noisy neighbour on node-g28 (high PCIe RX error rate).
sam: quick mitigation suggestion: reduce autoscaler burst threshold from 40 to 25 and temporarily bump warm-fork pool size by +3 for ded-pool-3. Also tweak batching heuristic to allow joiner to coalesce for an extra 20ms to avoid tiny-batch thrashing. Thoughts? :thinking_face:
jin: agree on warm-fork bump. For batching, we should gate the extra delay only when joiner queue > 20 to avoid harming latency in normal load. I'll open a PR.
perf-bot: profiling summary (auto): top contributors to p99 increase: 1) kernel fallback overhead +18ms, 2) KV rewarm (misses) +12ms, 3) joiner hysteresis -> tiny batches +9ms. Baseline vs window attached.
ops-bot: canary deploy triggered: config/changsets/193210-hotfix-batching deployed to ded-pool-3 canary=2/10 at 11:18Z.
ryan: after canary, observed immediate reduction in tiny-batch ratio (from 39%->11%) and p99 trending down. KV miss rate still elevated on some shards — likely due to rebalancer moving state off noisy node.
jin: root causes we're tracking: (A) noisy neighbor causing node-level errors -> provisioning jitter, (B) kernel selection incompatibility path that causes expensive fallback, (C) batching hysteresis too aggressive when handoff latency spikes.
maya: short-term runbook: 1) scale warm-fork +3 on ded-pool-3 (sam) 2) revert autoscaler burst to safer =25 (sam) 3) canary batching tweak (jin) 4) cordon node-g28 and migrate shards (anita) 5) open eval on kernel compat path (ryan).
anita: cordon + shard migration scheduled, ETA 11:46Z.
sam: done with warm-fork bump and autoscaler config updated.
jin: PR 2319 opened: batching gate when joiner_len>20, +20ms coalesce window. Attaching quick tests in PR.
perf-bot: post-change snapshot: p99 down to 1.1x baseline, throughput recovered to 98% of expected peak. Marking incident as "mitigated" pending root-cause PRs.
maya: nice work team. Next actions: ryan to dig into kernel selector heuristics (why compat_check flipped), jin to extend fallback telemetry, anita to validate node health after migration. I'll write the post-incident note. Assign owners and ETA for fixes. :thumbsup:
jin: noted, will include a small telemetry field: kernel_compat_last_success_ts and fallback_count_per_model.
ryan: I'll run a reproducible profile with the failing quant path and file an RCA draft by EOD.
maya: Thanks — closing thread for now, will add links to postmortem when ready.
